event: The United States announced that Israel and Lebanon agreed to extend their ceasefire for 45 days, with political negotiations scheduled to begin on May 29 and security negotiations on June 2.

verified_facts.statement: The United States announced a 45-day ceasefire extension between Israel and Lebanon
verified_facts.note: Standard diplomatic announcement; date and duration are concrete and verifiable

verified_facts.statement: Political negotiations were scheduled to begin on May 29
verified_facts.note: Announced negotiation date; verifiable against official US State Department records

verified_facts.statement: Security negotiations were scheduled to begin on June 2
verified_facts.note: Announced negotiation date; verifiable against official US State Department records

verified_facts.statement: Israel and Lebanon have engaged in direct bilateral talks
verified_facts.note: Confirmed by multiple official sources; the fact of engagement is not disputed

verified_facts.statement: Israeli military forces remain present in Lebanese territory
verified_facts.note: Documented by UN observers and multiple news sources; not disputed by any framing

verified_facts.statement: Hezbollah was not included as a direct party to the negotiations
verified_facts.note: Confirmed across all framings; structural fact about negotiation format

unverified_shared_claims.statement: Hundreds of Lebanese civilians have been killed since the ceasefire took effect
unverified_shared_claims.note: The 'Human Cost' framing cites 657+ killed per Health Ministry; other framings do not dispute the deaths but contest whether they occurred 'under ceasefire' or represent ceasefire violations. The exact number and attribution require verification against Lebanese Health Ministry and independent sources.

unverified_shared_claims.statement: Over 1 million people have been displaced
unverified_shared_claims.note: Cited in 'Human Cost' framing; requires verification against UNHCR, Lebanese government, and humanitarian organization records

unverified_shared_claims.statement: Israeli Defense Minister Katz publicly denied that ceasefire terms apply
unverified_shared_claims.note: Cited in 'Ceasefire-in-Name-Only' framing; requires verification against Israeli government statements and news archives
Attributed to Qassem in 'Hezbollah Disarmament' framing; requires verification against Hezbollah statements and news sources

unverified_shared_claims.statement: This is the first direct Israel-Lebanon engagement since 1993 (or 1983)
unverified_shared_claims.note: Claimed in 'Historic Diplomatic Milestone' framing; the exact date of last direct talks requires historical verification

unverified_shared_claims.statement: Lebanon ceasefire violations caused US-Iran talks to collapse in early June 2026
unverified_shared_claims.note: Cited in 'Iran Linkage' framing; this is a causal claim about future events that requires verification against diplomatic records

points_of_disagreement: Whether the ceasefire is genuine or a 'fiction' masking continued active conflict
Whether civilian deaths constitute violations of the ceasefire or evidence the ceasefire never took effect
Whether the exclusion of Hezbollah from talks is a strength (enabling Israeli-Lebanese state-to-state progress) or a fatal weakness (ensuring Hezbollah veto power)
Whether the ceasefire represents US diplomatic success or a temporary pause in an unresolved conflict
Whether Hezbollah disarmament is achievable through this framework or impossible without Hezbollah's consent
Whether the talks represent a historic structural shift toward Lebanese sovereignty or a coercive framework imposed on Lebanon
Whether the ceasefire can be separated from broader Iran-US conflict dynamics or is inherently linked to them
Whether Israeli troop presence is a temporary security measure or an occupation that undermines Lebanese sovereignty
Whether the framework empowers the Lebanese state or bypasses it by excluding its major political-military actor
shared_foundation.summary: All framings accept that a 45-day ceasefire extension was announced, direct Israel-Lebanon talks are scheduled, Hezbollah was excluded from negotiations, and Israeli forces remain in Lebanon. The disagreement centers on whether this framework represents genuine progress toward peace or a diplomatic label on continued conflict, whether Hezbollah's exclusion enables or dooms the talks, and whether civilian deaths constitute ceasefire violations or evidence the ceasefire never functioned.

framings.name: US Diplomatic Triumph
framings.question: Is this ceasefire extension a vindication of Trump-era deal-making and American diplomatic leadership in the Middle East?
framings.key_claim: The 45-day ceasefire extension and dual-track negotiations prove that American power brokering under Trump is producing tangible progress toward lasting peace where previous administrations failed.
framings.description: This framing presents the ceasefire extension as a signature achievement of Trump administration diplomacy, emphasizing that Washington convened the first direct Israel-Lebanon talks in decades and is now running parallel political and military tracks.
framings.emphasizes: The historic nature of direct Israel-Lebanon talks, US as indispensable mediator, the two-track structure (Pentagon security track + State Dept political track), Trump personally restraining Netanyahu, progress toward sovereignty and Hezbollah disarmament.
framings.downplays: Ongoing Israeli strikes during the ceasefire, Hezbollah's exclusion from talks and its outright rejection of terms, the fragility and prior violations of the truce, high civilian death tolls under the ceasefire.
sample_headlines: Israel and Lebanon Agree to 45-Day Extension of Ceasefire, U.S. State Department Says
Israel-Lebanon Agree On 45-Day Ceasefire Extension, Pentagon 'Security Track' On May 29: US State Department

carriers.name: US State Department / Tommy Pigott
carriers.excerpt: "The two countries agreed upon a framework for negotiations to advance lasting peace between the two countries, full recognition of each other's sovereignty and territorial integrity"
carriers.role_evidence: State Dept spokesperson Pigott coined the 'highly productive' and 'two-track' framing in the official announcement

carriers.name: Just The News
carriers.excerpt: "Trump stated at the time that 'The United States is going to work with Lebanon in order to help it protect itself from Hezbollah'"
carriers.role_evidence: Framed the ceasefire as a Trump-led diplomatic win with minimal critique of ongoing strikes

carriers.name: CNBC
carriers.excerpt: "Israel and Lebanon agreed to extend their ceasefire by three weeks following a meeting in the White House with top U.S. officials, President Donald Trump said"
carriers.role_evidence: Amplified Trump's personal announcement framing to a broad financial/general audience

carriers.name: Donald Trump (Truth Social)
carriers.excerpt: "The United States is going to work with Lebanon in order to help it protect itself from Hezbollah"
carriers.role_evidence: Trump personally announced extensions on Truth Social, lending presidential authority to the triumph framing

carriers.name: MS NOW
carriers.excerpt: "These two states have crossed a Rubicon"
carriers.role_evidence: Anonymous US official source described the talks as crossing a historical threshold, amplifying the triumph frame with insider sourcing

framings.name: Ceasefire-in-Name-Only / Enforcement Failure
framings.question: Does the ceasefire extension actually mean anything when fighting continues daily and violations go unpunished?
framings.key_claim: The 45-day extension is a diplomatic fiction because Israeli strikes and Hezbollah fire have continued throughout, turning the ceasefire into a political label on an active war.
framings.description: This framing interrogates whether the ceasefire has any operational meaning, documenting the gap between announced agreements and ground reality — strikes, deaths, and violations persist regardless of extension announcements.
framings.emphasizes: Hundreds killed under active 'ceasefires', Hezbollah's exclusion as a wild card, Israeli strikes continuing after each agreement, Israel Defense Minister Katz publicly denying ceasefire terms apply, the pattern of repeated short extensions masking stasis.
framings.downplays: Diplomatic progress achieved, the structural complexity of getting a non-state actor to comply, US efforts to restrain Netanyahu.
sample_headlines: Conflict Grinds on in Lebanon Despite a 'Ceasefire' — The Soufan Center
Gaza, Iran, Lebanon: If Ceasefires Are in Place, Why Do Strikes Continue? — Al Jazeera
Israel-Lebanon Ceasefire Extended by 45 Days but Deadly Strikes Continue — The National

carriers.name: The Soufan Center
carriers.excerpt: "the seemingly intractable combat in South Lebanon continues despite a formal ceasefire announced in April, which exists in name only"
carriers.role_evidence: Coined the 'exists in name only' characterization of the ceasefire, grounded in detailed enforcement analysis

carriers.name: Al Jazeera
carriers.excerpt: "Israel's attacks on Lebanon continue unchecked, with strikes on the Naqoura and Nabatieh districts of southern Lebanon"
carriers.role_evidence: Published a dedicated explainer amplifying the enforcement-failure framing to a global audience with expert citations

carriers.name: The National News
carriers.excerpt: "The announcement came as Israeli strikes continued across southern Lebanon overnight and into Saturday"
carriers.role_evidence: Juxtaposed the ceasefire announcement directly against same-day strike reporting, establishing the contradiction frame

carriers.name: NPR / Brian Katulis (Middle East Institute)
carriers.excerpt: "These ceasefires between Israel and Hezbollah essentially have been quite tenuous, and they've been broken almost on a daily basis"
carriers.role_evidence: Expert analyst on NPR provided the 'daily breach' characterization that anchored the enforcement-failure frame for US public radio audiences

carriers.name: Michael Lynk / Al Jazeera
carriers.excerpt: "ceasefires are ultimately political documents because it requires political will to enforce them"
carriers.role_evidence: International law scholar provided academic grounding for the enforcement-failure framing

framings.name: Human Cost / Civilian Harm
framings.question: Who is being killed and displaced under this ceasefire, and is the international community doing enough about it?
framings.key_claim: Hundreds of Lebanese civilians — including medical workers, women, and children — have been killed by Israeli strikes since the ceasefire took effect, constituting a humanitarian catastrophe that diplomatic announcements obscure.
framings.description: This framing centers the physical toll on Lebanese civilians and displaced persons, using casualty data from Lebanon's Health Ministry and UN bodies to argue that diplomacy is providing cover for ongoing harm rather than stopping it.
framings.emphasizes: Death tolls (657+ killed under ceasefire per Health Ministry), displacement of over 1 million people, strikes on health infrastructure, paramedics killed, Lebanese President Aoun condemning 'continuing violations', UN expert condemnations.
framings.downplays: Hezbollah's military role in triggering Israeli responses, Israeli security rationale for strikes, diplomatic progress toward a longer-term framework.
sample_headlines: UN Experts Condemn Israel's Unprecedented Bombing in Lebanon After Ceasefire Announcement — OHCHR
Israel-Lebanon Ceasefire Extended by 45 Days but Deadly Strikes Continue — The National
Since the Israel-Hezbollah Fighting Reignited in March, at Least 3,516 Have Been Killed in Lebanon — TIME

carriers.name: UN OHCHR (Special Rapporteurs)
carriers.excerpt: "Many strikes hit densely populated residential neighbourhoods and commercial areas in central Beirut in violation of the principles of distinction and proportionality"
carriers.role_evidence: First major institutional body to frame the strikes as IHL violations and demand arms embargo, establishing the human cost/accountability frame

carriers.name: Lebanon Ministry of Public Health
carriers.excerpt: "more than 3,500 women, men, and children were killed by Israeli strikes in Lebanon" since March 2
carriers.role_evidence: Primary data source repeatedly cited across all outlets to anchor the civilian harm frame with authoritative casualty figures

carriers.name: TIME
carriers.excerpt: "at least 3,516 have been killed in Lebanon, with 10,674 wounded, according to the country's Health Ministry"
carriers.role_evidence: Widely-read outlet that foregrounded the cumulative casualty toll in its ceasefire coverage

carriers.name: Al Jazeera (Manuel Rapalo / Ziad Majed)
carriers.excerpt: "The Israelis are interpreting the agreement as just another one to allow them to continue their attacks"
carriers.role_evidence: Amplified academic and analyst voices challenging Israel's framing of strikes as ceasefire-compliant to a global audience

carriers.name: Lebanese President Joseph Aoun
carriers.excerpt: "despite the ceasefire, demolitions of homes and places of worship, while the number of killed and wounded rises day after day"
carriers.role_evidence: Head of state formally adopted the civilian-harm framing in official condemnations of Israeli strikes

framings.name: Hezbollah Disarmament as the Central Test
framings.question: Can and will Lebanon disarm Hezbollah, and is the ceasefire framework a credible mechanism for achieving that goal?
framings.key_claim: The ceasefire extension is only meaningful if it produces concrete Hezbollah disarmament; without it, the talks will cycle endlessly because Hezbollah — excluded from negotiations — retains veto power over any agreement.
framings.description: This security-analytical framing treats the ceasefire extension primarily as a vehicle for Hezbollah disarmament, assessing whether the Lebanese Armed Forces have the will and capacity to act, and whether Hezbollah will comply or spoil the process.
framings.emphasizes: Hezbollah's exclusion from talks, Qassem's explicit rejection of disarmament, Lebanon's sovereign authority question, the 'ball is in Lebanon's court' pressure on Beirut, the Pentagon security track as a disarmament tool, Syria's removal from the Hezbollah supply chain as a structural advantage.
framings.downplays: Ongoing Israeli violations of the ceasefire, civilian casualties, the political infeasibility of forcing disarmament without triggering civil conflict in Lebanon.
sample_headlines: As Israel and Lebanon Extend Ceasefire by 45 Days, Hezbollah Disarmament Remains Elusive — MS NOW
With Talks, the U.S., Lebanon, and Israel Try to Isolate Hezbollah and Iran — The Soufan Center
Lebanon's Second Chance — Foundation for Defense of Democracies

carriers.name: MS NOW
carriers.excerpt: "Both parties still agree on the same goals of disarming Hezbollah — but they're not able to talk about how they get to the same goal"
carriers.role_evidence: Framed the entire ceasefire story around the disarmament gap in the headline and throughout, using exclusive sourcing

carriers.name: The Soufan Center
carriers.excerpt: "Lebanon, Israel, and the U.S. are aligned in seeking Hezbollah's disarmament and demobilization"
carriers.role_evidence: Think-tank analysis consistently foregrounded disarmament as the strategic linchpin of the entire ceasefire architecture

carriers.name: Foundation for Defense of Democracies (FDD)
carriers.excerpt: "Israel will likely continue disarming Hezbollah unilaterally through overflights, targeted operations, and retention of strategic buffer zones"
carriers.role_evidence: Published detailed pro-Israel security analysis arguing disarmament is a prerequisite, not a product, of any ceasefire

carriers.name: Israeli PM Benjamin Netanyahu
carriers.excerpt: "we want the dismantling of Hezbollah's weapons, and we want a real peace agreement that will last for generations"
carriers.role_evidence: Official Israeli government position made disarmament the explicit precondition for any comprehensive agreement

carriers.name: Security Council Report
carriers.excerpt: "Many Council members have accused Hezbollah of dragging Lebanon into a confrontation that the Lebanese population did not seek"
carriers.role_evidence: UN Security Council monitoring body documented international consensus around Hezbollah disarmament as Lebanon sovereignty issue

carriers.name: Hezbollah / Naim Qassem
carriers.excerpt: "We are concerned only with a comprehensive cessation of aggression, a cease-fire, and the withdrawal of Israel"
carriers.role_evidence: Hezbollah explicitly rejected the disarmament-centric framing, calling compliance 'surrender' and reframing around Israeli withdrawal

framings.name: Lebanese Sovereignty and State Empowerment
framings.question: Does this ceasefire create a genuine path to Lebanese state authority over its own territory, or does it entrench both Israeli occupation and Hezbollah's parallel state?
framings.key_claim: The ceasefire extension is Lebanon's historic opportunity to reclaim full sovereignty by asserting the Lebanese Armed Forces as the sole security actor — but that opportunity is undermined by both Israeli troop presence and Hezbollah's refusal to disarm.
framings.description: This framing, prominent among Lebanese government voices and some Western diplomats, treats the ceasefire as a sovereignty question — whether Lebanon can emerge from the conflict as a fully functioning state free from both Israeli occupation and Hezbollah's armed dominance.
framings.emphasizes: Lebanon's diplomatic assertiveness under President Aoun and PM Salam, the 'pilot zones' concept for LAF exclusive control, Lebanon's rejection of Iran negotiating on its behalf, the historic nature of direct talks since 1983, displacement of civilians and urgency of reconstruction.
framings.downplays: Lebanon's limited capacity to confront Hezbollah, internal political fragility, the degree to which Beirut's negotiating position depends on US and Israeli restraint.
sample_headlines: Lebanon's Embassy Says Talks Yielded 'Meaningful Diplomatic Progress' — The National
Lebanon Reaffirmed Necessity for Mutual Respect of Internationally Recognized Borders — US State Dept Joint Statement

carriers.name: Lebanese Embassy in Washington / Lebanon President Aoun
carriers.excerpt: "Our objective is to transform the current ceasefire momentum into a comprehensive and lasting agreement that safeguards the dignity, security, and future of the Lebanese people"
carriers.role_evidence: Lebanese Embassy statement first articulated the sovereignty-restoration goal as the defining purpose of the ceasefire extension

carriers.name: US State Department (Joint Statement)
carriers.excerpt: "All countries reaffirmed that the future of the relationship between Israel and Lebanon must be decided by the two sovereign governments"
carriers.role_evidence: Official US-Israel-Lebanon joint statement codified the sovereignty frame as a formal three-party commitment

carriers.name: The Soufan Center
carriers.excerpt: "Beirut seeks to favorably contrast its approach with the costly strategy of unending 'resistance' advocated by Hezbollah"
carriers.role_evidence: Analytical framing of Beirut's strategy as a deliberate sovereignty bid, not just compliance with US pressure

carriers.name: MS NOW (quoting State Dept official)
carriers.excerpt: "The time has come to treat Lebanon as a sovereign state and to finally empower it to act like one"
carriers.role_evidence: Circulated the US official framing of Lebanon-as-sovereign-actor to a wide readership, amplifying the empowerment narrative

carriers.name: Hezbollah / Naim Qassem
carriers.excerpt: "direct negotiations represent 'concessions by Lebanese authorities'"
carriers.role_evidence: Qassem explicitly challenged the sovereignty framing, arguing Beirut was capitulating rather than asserting independence

framings.name: Iran Linkage / Regional Conflict Architecture
framings.question: Can the Israel-Lebanon ceasefire be sustained in isolation from the US-Iran war, or are they inextricably linked in ways the Trump administration is denying?
framings.key_claim: Attempts to separate the Lebanon ceasefire from the broader US-Iran conflict are artificial — Iran controls Hezbollah's calculus, and progress in Lebanon will collapse whenever the Iran talks stall or escalate.
framings.description: This geopolitical framing treats the Lebanon ceasefire as a subsidiary theater of the wider regional war, arguing that the fundamental drivers (Iran's proxy strategy, the US-Iran nuclear/military confrontation, Strait of Hormuz dynamics) will determine whether any Lebanon deal holds.
framings.emphasizes: Iran's demand that Lebanon be included in any Iran-US ceasefire, Tehran's threat to resume war if Israel strikes Beirut, Hezbollah's strategic value to Iran, Trump's insistence on separating the tracks, the way Lebanon ceasefire violations blew up US-Iran talks in early June 2026.
framings.downplays: Lebanon's independent political agency, the possibility that post-Assad Syrian dynamics have structurally weakened Hezbollah's Iran supply chain, the merits of a bilateral Israel-Lebanon track.
sample_headlines: Ceasefire Falters as Israel and Iran Trade Worst Strikes in Months — CNN
Israel and Lebanon Extend Ceasefire 45 Days After Washington Talks — Bloomberg
Iran Insists Conflicts Are Linked; Tehran Warns Attack on Beirut Would Trigger Full-Scale Resumption — Al Jazeera

carriers.name: Bloomberg
carriers.excerpt: "the Trump administration tries to tamp down a conflict that's made ending the war against Iran more difficult"
carriers.role_evidence: Bloomberg was among the first major financial/news outlets to explicitly frame the Lebanon ceasefire as a complicating factor in the US-Iran war, not a standalone event

carriers.name: CNN
carriers.excerpt: "The hostilities also complicate fragile truces and peace deal negotiations"
carriers.role_evidence: Live-blogged the collapse of the Lebanon ceasefire alongside Iran escalation, visually dramatizing the linkage for mass audiences

carriers.name: PBS NewsHour / AP
carriers.excerpt: "tensions remain high and threaten to tip the Middle East back into open warfare and prolong the worldwide energy crisis"
carriers.role_evidence: Embedded the Lebanon ceasefire announcement inside the Iran-war context, explicitly linking the two conflicts in its lede

carriers.name: Iran Foreign Ministry / Abbas Araghchi
carriers.excerpt: "any attack on Beirut would trigger a 'full-scale resumption' of war"
carriers.role_evidence: Iran officially adopted the linkage framing as state policy, threatening escalation if Lebanon-Iran conflict separation was imposed

carriers.name: Donald Trump / ABC News
carriers.excerpt: "Trump said he wanted to separate talks on the conflict in Lebanon and those on the US-Israeli war on Iran"
carriers.role_evidence: Trump explicitly pushed back on the linkage framing, insisting Lebanon could be de-coupled from the Iran track — making him the primary critic of this framing

framings.name: Historic Diplomatic Milestone
framings.question: Does this represent a genuinely unprecedented opening for Israel-Lebanon normalization after decades of hostility and failed agreements?
framings.key_claim: For the first time since the failed May 17 Agreement of 1983, Israel and Lebanon are engaged in direct bilateral talks that could produce a durable peace — a structural shift, not just a tactical pause.
framings.description: This long-view framing situates the ceasefire extension within the deep history of Israel-Lebanon relations, treating the direct ambassador-level talks and dual-track framework as potentially transformative for bilateral normalization regardless of near-term ceasefire fragility.
framings.emphasizes: First direct Israel-Lebanon engagement since 1993, first peace talks since 1983, Lebanese PM Salam's openness to 'any agenda, format or location', the 43-year diplomatic gap being bridged, European and international welcome for the process, the structural weakening of Hezbollah.
framings.downplays: Ongoing military violations, Hezbollah's spoiler capacity, Iranian opposition, the extent to which talks are driven by Israeli military pressure rather than genuine mutual interest.
sample_headlines: Israel and Lebanon Announce Opening of Direct Negotiations for the First Time Since 1983 — Wikipedia / Reuters (cited)
The Ceasefire Marked the First Direct Diplomatic Engagement Between Israel and Lebanon in Decades — The Soufan Center

carriers.name: Reuters / AP (as cited in multiple outlets)
carriers.excerpt: "historic"; noted support from Lebanese President Joseph Aoun, who called for the talks
carriers.role_evidence: Wire services first applied the 'historic' label to the announcement of direct talks, setting the tone adopted by downstream outlets

carriers.name: The Soufan Center
carriers.excerpt: "the first official talks since 1993"
carriers.role_evidence: Provided the historical context that transformed a ceasefire announcement into a structural milestone framing

carriers.name: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen
carriers.excerpt: "welcomed the agreement and emphasized its importance in reducing violence and enabling humanitarian relief"
carriers.role_evidence: European institutional endorsement reinforced the milestone framing at the highest international level

carriers.name: Israeli Ambassador Yechiel Leiter (X / social media)
carriers.excerpt: "There will be ups and downs, but the potential for success is great"
carriers.role_evidence: Israeli ambassador used social media to amplify the historic-progress framing directly to English-speaking audiences after the 45-day extension

carriers.name: Lebanon President Aoun / PM Salam
carriers.excerpt: "the only solution to the situation in Lebanon is a ceasefire with Israel that will lead to direct negotiations between the two countries"
carriers.role_evidence: Lebanese government officially embraced the milestone framing, contrasting it with Lebanon's historical reliance on Iran/Syria as intermediaries

framings.name: Hezbollah Resistance / Anti-Capitulation
framings.question: Are Lebanon's government and the US pressuring a sovereign people into an imposed settlement that legitimizes Israeli occupation and dismantles legitimate resistance?
framings.key_claim: The US-brokered ceasefire framework is a capitulation to Israeli and American demands that bypasses Hezbollah — a major political and military actor — and will not produce a durable peace because it is built on coercion rather than consent.
framings.description: This framing, advanced primarily by Hezbollah and Iran, frames the negotiations as an externally imposed process that excludes the primary military actor, legitimizes Israeli occupation of Lebanese territory, and demands unilateral disarmament without Israeli withdrawal.
framings.emphasizes: Hezbollah's exclusion from talks, Israeli troops remaining on Lebanese soil, the demand for withdrawal as a precondition for any deal, Iran's argument that Lebanon's future cannot be decided without Hezbollah, continued Hezbollah military operations as legitimate resistance.
framings.downplays: Hezbollah's role in triggering the 2026 escalation, the Lebanese government's own declared desire to disarm Hezbollah, the civilian suffering caused by Hezbollah's rocket attacks on northern Israel.
sample_headlines: Hezbollah Rejects Israel-Lebanon Ceasefire Agreement — TIME / AFP
Hezbollah Leader Naim Qassem: Withdrawal from Southern Lebanon Means 'Surrender, Defeat and Achieving the Enemy's Goals'

carriers.name: Hezbollah / Naim Qassem (Al-Manar TV)
carriers.excerpt: "What we are concerned about is an end to the aggression, ceasefire and Israel's withdrawal"
carriers.role_evidence: Qassem's televised rejection statement first fully articulated the anti-capitulation framing in response to the ceasefire terms

carriers.name: Iran Foreign Ministry / Araghchi
carriers.excerpt: "The world must recognize that Hezbollah is part of Lebanon's reality"
carriers.role_evidence: Iranian foreign minister institutionally adopted the legitimacy framing, demanding Hezbollah's inclusion in any settlement

carriers.name: Hezbollah MP Hussein Hajj Hassan
carriers.excerpt: "Neither they nor anyone else will be able to carry out what the enemy wants, especially when it comes to the issue of disarming the resistance"
carriers.role_evidence: Hezbollah's parliamentary wing amplified Qassem's rejection publicly, broadening the anti-capitulation messaging beyond the Secretary-General

carriers.name: Nabih Berri (Parliament Speaker / Hezbollah ally)
carriers.excerpt: Berri passed on Hezbollah's rejection to the Lebanese government, "shares this position"
carriers.role_evidence: As parliament speaker, Berri gave the anti-capitulation framing institutional resonance within Lebanon's formal political structure

carriers.name: Far-right Israeli ministers (Ben Gvir) — as inadvertent validators
carriers.excerpt: "Now is the time to tell our friend, President Trump, 'No'"
carriers.role_evidence: Far-right Israeli opposition to Trump's ceasefire pressure paradoxically validated Hezbollah's argument that the deal served neither resistance nor genuine Israeli security interests

gap_analysis: Missing: Israeli domestic political perspectives (right-wing security hawks questioning sufficiency of terms, left-wing doves cautiously optimistic, settler/border community concerns). Missing: Lebanese civil society and business community views on reconstruction timelines and economic recovery prospects. Missing: Technical/implementation framings—what specific mechanisms, verification protocols, or third-party enforcement structures exist, and do they work? Missing: Sunni Arab state perspectives (Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt) on regional balance-of-power shifts and their own security interests in the outcome.
